annotation.speech2: Five concentric circles centred at the origin in the x y plane, each drawn in a different colour, with a legend in the upper right giving the value of c on each. The values step down by one half, from c equals one half on the innermost circle to c equals negative three halves on the outermost.
The level curve where f equals one half, a circle of radius one over root two. It is the innermost circle, so the largest values of f occur near the origin.
The level curve where f equals zero, the unit circle.
The level curve where f equals negative one half, a circle of radius root three over two.
The level curve where f equals negative one, a circle of radius root two.

The level curve where f equals negative three halves, a circle of radius root five over two. Because c steps down by the same amount from one circle to the next, the circles crowd closer together further out, which tells us the surface is steepest near the rim.
